title: EVerest federated testing extra contract
description: Contract for results.extra in an EVerest federated testing CTRF submission. CTRF types extra as a bare object, so this file is what gives a submission meaning beyond pass/fail counts. Deliberately minimal: only build and integrator are required, so the cost of submitting at all stays low and everything beyond the build stays optional.

build.description: Build status. Carried here, NOT as a synthetic CTRF test. The intake gate rejects a submission whose build is missing or failed.

status.description: Overall build outcome. 'failed' submissions are rejected by the intake gate.

targets.description: Per-target results. EVerest itself cross-builds four embedded targets, so build status is plural by nature.

target.description: Target triple. The five in schema/vocabulary.json are the ones EVerest itself builds, so reporting one of those is directly comparable with upstream; anything else must still be a well-formed triple.

toolchain.description: Compiler and version, as '<compiler> <version>' - e.g. 'gcc 13.2.0', 'clang 18.1.0'. Standardised so toolchain can be compared across integrators rather than parsed by hand.

modules.description: EVerest modules built. Required: without it a submission cannot say which parts of EVerest it actually exercised, so two passing runs covering different module sets look identical. Checked against schema/everest-modules.txt and warned on if unknown.

items.description: EVerest module name, PascalCase, as under modules/**/. Checked against schema/everest-modules.txt and WARNED on if unknown - warn not reject, because the list drifts with EVerest.

integrator.description: Who submitted this. There is no native CTRF field for submitter identity.

id.description: Unique integrator id. Also the results/<id>/ directory name, which is what makes it unique under PR intake; under repository_dispatch it MUST be derived from the submitting token rather than self-declared, or uniqueness is unenforceable. Use a pseudonym to stay anonymous - there is no separate publication flag, because the repository is public.

displayName.description: Human-readable name. Omit to remain anonymous.

hardware.description: Hardware under test. Only meaningful when environment.testEnvironment is HIL. Per-test hardware belongs in the native test.device field instead.

bsp.description: Board support package or firmware identifier for the board itself, e.g. yeti-fw-1.4.2. NOT an EVerest module name - the modules a run exercised go in build.modules.

board.description: Board MODEL, e.g. yeti-1.1. This is the closest thing CTRF has to a device identity, and it is a model rather than a rig: two rigs with the same board are indistinguishable in a CTRF submission. Required when testEnvironment is HIL.

chargeController.description: Charge controller model or firmware, if it is a separate unit from the board.
